title: Inquest into shooting death to begin Nov. 8
article: The B.C. Coroner's Service is gearing up for a four-day inquest into the death of Langford musician Joseph Pagnotta, who was shot dead in a confrontation with police last February.
A five-person jury will listen to testimony from witnesses and then be asked to make recommendations on how to prevent future deaths and any changes that might help police handle similar incidents.
Regional coroner Rose Stanton has set aside Nov. 8, 9, 10 and 11 at the Victoria court house for the inquest.
The 52-year-old father of two was shot and killed Feb. 24 after he lunged at officers with a knife outside his Phelps Avenue duplex he shared with his wife of 20 years, Natasha.
Police initially tried to shock Pagnotta into submission with a electric stun-gun known as a Taser, but the device failed to stop him.
Pagnotta, a drummer who was well-known on the local music scene, had a history of drug addiction and mental illness.
He was released from a short stint in prison on fraud charges two weeks before his death.
Pagnotta had been diagnosed with chronic depression, but family members say he stopped taking his medication and started talking about suicide in the days leading up to his confrontation with police.
Pagnotta had a history of small-time drug dealing dating back a decade or more.
In 1995 he made news when an angry customer poured gasoline on Pagnotta and set him on fire. He spent a month recovering in hospital and was eventually handed a one year sentence for dealing cocaine.
One day before the shooting, Natasha Pagnotta fled the family home with her 12-year-old daughter for fear her suicidal husband would hurt himself or someone else.
Pagnotta also left behind 18-year-old son who was not living at the family home at the time of the shooting.
